  PRESENTATIONS
  1.  Employee Service Pin Awards
  Recommendation: Recognize July 2026 Employee Service Pin Award recipients.

  Human Resources Director Tan presented the staff report and the City Council
  recognized the 2026 Employee Service Pin Award recipients: Gas Systems
  Technician, Rodolfo Perez and Information Technology Manager, Ernesto Smith.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  2.  Conditional Use Permit for Dyrt Labs, Inc to Operate an Indoor Food Waste
  Composting Facility at 2550 27th Street
  Recommendation: A. Conduct a Public Hearing; B. Find that the proposed project
  is categorically exempt from California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review
  pursuant to Class 32 In-Fill Developments (CEQA Guidelines 15332) and there is
  no substantial evidence demonstrating that an exception to categorical exemption
  pursuant to CEQA Guidelines, Section 15300.2 applies, as the project is consistent
  with the general plan, and the zoning code, the property is less than five (5) acres
  in size and is surrounded by compatible industrial uses, has no value as habitat
  for endangered, rare or threatened species, no significant adverse impacts from
  traffic, parking, noise, dust, dust, air quality, or water quality are expected to occur
  from this project, and the site can be adequately served by all required utilities and
  public services; and C. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-038 approving a Conditional
  Use Permit allowing Dyrt Labs, Inc to operate an indoor food waste composting
  facility at 2550 27th Street and making certain findings as necessary.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra opened the public hearing at 9:17 a.m. There being no speakers,
  Mayor Ybarra closed the public hearing at 9:17 a.m.

  Mayor Ybarra invited further Council discussion. Council Member Larios inquired
  how hazardous materials would be handled and how the proposed facility would
  differ from existing waste management facilities. Public Works Director Wall
  responded that the facility would only accept organic materials.

  Health and Environmental Control Director Petrosyan also reassured Council that
  the Health Department would be conducting quarterly inspections. Staff would
  inform Council if any hazardous materials were to be brought in during any future
  instances.

  Lee Robinson of Dyrt Labs, Inc provided a summary of the operations of the
  proposed facility. He announced that all composting would be “in-vessel aerobic
  composting” and most of the waste would be provided by food distributors already
  located within city boundaries.

  Mayor Ybarra reopened the public hearing at 9:25 a.m. There being no speakers,
  Mayor Ybarra closed the public hearing at 9:25 a.m.

  Council requested available closeout reports on the applicant’s past experiences.
  Health and Environmental Control Director Petrosyan announced that the Health
  Department has enforcement power to address any potential odors that may be
  caused by the applicant’s operations.

  City Administrator Saeki noted that the conditional use permit can be further
  modified to incorporate new or more stringent conditions to mitigate any potential
  odors.

  Mayor Ybarra called for a motion.

  MOTION
  Mayor Ybarra moved and Council Member Larios seconded a motion to table the
  item to the September 15, 2026 City Council meeting with updated findings and
  recommendations pertaining to the conditional use permit. The question was called
  and the motion carried unanimously.

  NEW BUSINESS

  18.  Regular Vernon City Council Meeting Times
  Recommendation: Discuss meeting times for regular meetings of the City Council
  and provide direction to staff regarding potential changes.

  City Administrator Saeki presented the staff report and provided options for
  Regular City Council meeting times. Mayor Ybarra said she would like to try
  different times during a test period. Council Member Larios said she would like to
  see more candidates apply for City Council, and that a later meeting time would
  allow more public participation and more council candidates. Council Member
  Merlo added that she would want business representatives to be able to attend
  public meetings.

  City Attorney Moussa-Milward added that the City Council should try to minimize
  the test period because certain items cannot be approved during special meetings.
  Discussion ensued among the City Council.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments.

  Marisa Olguin, President of the Vernon Chamber of Commerce, noted that holding
  meetings at 4 p.m. would facilitate attendance from the business community and
  allow residents to engage.

  The City Council agreed to move forward with the test meeting times, including
  one special meeting a month at 4:00 p.m. to gauge engagement.

  City Administrator Saeki clarified Council’s test period requirements: 1) Each first
  meeting of the month would be a special meeting beginning at 4:00 p.m., and the
  second meeting of each month would remain at 9:00 a.m. 2) Information regarding
  the testing period would be brought back for Council consideration during the
  second City Council meeting in January. 3) The testing period would commence in
  September or October, pending a final review of upcoming business items from
  staff.

  Mayor Ybarra invited additional public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra
  called for a motion.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to proceed with Council’s direction for test meeting times. The question was called
  and the motion carried unanimously.

  19.  Zoning: Permitted Use Cross-Reference Matrix
  Recommendation: A. Receive and file the Permitted Use Cross-Reference Matrix;
  and B. Provide direction to staff on any desired amendments to Title 17 of the
  Vernon Municipal Code to reclassify certain land uses currently allowed by-right to
  require a higher level of discretionary review through Conditional Use Permits or
  Development Agreements.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments.

  Marisa Olguin, President of the Vernon Chamber of Commerce, asked that the City
  Council to be cautious about the types of uses authorized within the City.

  Discussion ensued among the City Council. Council directed staff to add cold
  storage centers and data centers to the list of uses that may require a higher level
  of discretionary review through Conditional Use Permits or Development
  Agreements.

  MOTION
  Mayor Ybarra moved and Council Member Merlo seconded a motion to bring back
  the item with Council’s recommendations. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  20.  Emergency Donations to Nonprofit Organizations Responding to the Palos
  Warehouse Fire
  A. Find that providing financial support to nonprofit organizations responding to the
  Palos Warehouse Fire serves a public purpose and benefits Vernon area
  communities; and
  B. Approve and authorize emergency donations in the amount of $10,000 each
  ($30,000 in total) to 1) InnerCity Struggle; 2) Labor Community Services Los
  Angeles; and 3) Proyecto Pastoral at Dolores Mission, nonprofit organizations that
  have provided aid to families and individuals affected by the Palos Warehouse Fire,
  and authorize the City Administrator to execute any related documentation to
  facilitate the donations.

  City Administrator Saeki presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments.
